clue.text: Hoarse by the sound of it

definitions.text: Hoarse by the sound of it

blocks.clueFragment: Hoarse by the sound of it
blocks.note: surface reading: a voice that sounds rough and husky

blocks.clueFragment: Hoarse by the sound of it
blocks.note: setter's reading: a game whose name, said aloud the British way, is the same as the adjective for a husky voice

explanation.walkthrough: One of the puzzle's unstated games: the lawn game with mallets and hoops, said aloud the British way, is close to croaky, which is what hoarse means.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue defines only by sound: the game's name echoes the adjective croaky, a synonym for husky or rough-voiced.

clue.text: Noisy episodes

blocks.note: surface reading: loud disturbances or rows
setter's reading: the plural word for such din is also an indoor court game played with a hard ball

explanation.walkthrough: The plural of a word for a din is also the name of an old court game related to squash, one of the puzzle's many games.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud commotion, so several loud disturbances are rackets in the plural.

clue.text: Question a sailor in the Middle East

definitions.note: the answer is a country in that region

blocks.note: Q is the standard abbreviation for question
taken as written
a tar is a sailor in crossword shorthand

explanation.surface: Interrogating a seaman somewhere in the Gulf region.
explanation.definitionFit: Qatar is a small emirate on a peninsula in the Persian Gulf, part of the region called the Middle East.

clue.text: Backer supports English version of the gospel

indicators.note: in a down answer, whatever supports something sits underneath it, so the backer comes after the other letters

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
V is the abbreviation for version
an angel is a financial backer, especially of a theatre show

explanation.surface: A sponsor funds an English translation of the scriptures.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'supports' means the backer sits underneath English and version.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangel is an old word for the gospel, the good news preached by Christian teaching.

clue.text: Choreographer keeps Wally in reserve

indicators.note: something that keeps another thing holds it within itself

blocks.note: a mine is a rich store or reserve to draw upon
a wally is British slang for a fool, as is an ass

explanation.surface: A dance director holds back some hapless man called Wally as a spare.
explanation.walkthrough: Wally looks like a man's name; in British slang it means an idiot. Léonide Massine was a Russian-born dancer and choreographer with the Ballets Russes.
explanation.definitionFit: Léonide Massine created many celebrated ballets for Diaghilev's company, so he is an example of a choreographer.

clue.text: Claim legal misrepresentation over a point

indicators.note: a misrepresentation presents things wrongly, so the letters are set out in a distorted order
in a down answer, being over something means sitting above it, so the shuffled word comes first

blocks.note: the anagram fodder
a compass point, east

explanation.surface: A lawyer accuses someone of twisting the law on a technicality.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert something as true without proof yet, the same verb as to claim.

clue.text: Colt's offspring may be a rogue

blocks.note: a son is offspring
a Colt is a make of revolver, and the possessive is read as of a gun

explanation.surface: A young horse's foal could turn out to be a scamp.
explanation.walkthrough: Colt looks like a young horse, but its capital marks the revolver maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Son of a gun is an old affectionate or mildly scornful phrase for a rascal or scoundrel.

clue.text: Clear delivery

definitions.note: the whole clue doubles as a picture of the game

blocks.note: to clear a sum is to net it as profit
in cricket each delivery from the bowler is a ball

explanation.walkthrough: One of the puzzle's unstated games. The whole clue builds the answer and also hints at it, since the game is all clean passing. A delivery is a cricket term for one bowled ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team game played by passing the ball cleanly and shooting through a high ring, so a clear delivery is its essence.

clue.text: Ray's getting on

definitions.note: the whole clue doubles as a playful picture of the sport

blocks.note: a skate is a kind of ray, the flat fish; the 's is read as is
boarding is getting on a ship, bus or train

explanation.surface: Someone called Ray is getting older.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the puzzle's unstated games, clued by wordplay alone. Ray reads as a man's name and 'getting on' as ageing; in fact ray is the fish and getting on means climbing aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: No words define it: riding a wheeled board is one of the puzzle's hidden set of sports and pastimes.

clue.text: Bob trimmed tail

blocks.note: a bob was an old British shilling, abbreviated S
trimmed means cut

explanation.surface: A bobtail is a tail that has been docked short.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was slang for a shilling, the pre-decimal British coin written s.
explanation.definitionFit: A scut is the short upright tail of a rabbit, hare or deer.

clue.text: Baseness of Tina and Lily frolicking with a king

indicators.note: frolicking is romping about playfully, so the letters jump into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Two girls behaving shamefully by cavorting with a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Baseness suggests moral lowness, but here it is the chemist's sense: being a base rather than an acid.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry a base is an alkali, so the quality of being basic is the property of being alkaline.

clue.text: King meets a German in an unploughed field

blocks.note: Shakespeare's King Lear
a is read as one, the Roman numeral I
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A monarch encounters a German visitor out in the fallow fields.
explanation.walkthrough: Lea-rig is a Scots word, known from a Burns song, for a grassy ridge left unploughed.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is grassland left unploughed and a rig is a ridge of a field, so the compound names fallow land.

clue.text: Battleship?

blocks.note: surface reading: a large armoured warship
setter's reading: a contest whose name suggests a little towing vessel belonging to warfare

explanation.walkthrough: Split the word as battle and ship: a vessel of combat is a small towboat of war, which is the name of the rope-pulling contest.
explanation.definitionFit: The rope-pulling sport is literally a struggle, and its name reads as a tugboat of war, a pun on a fighting vessel.

clue.text: Boer gets atlas reproduced as a navigational aid

indicators.note: something reproduced is made again, so the letters are reassembled in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A South African farmer gets a copy of a book of maps to find his way.
explanation.definitionFit: The astrolabe was an early instrument for measuring the height of stars, used by sailors to fix position.

clue.text: Grasping red wine found in border plunder

indicators.note: something found in another thing lies inside it

blocks.note: reiving was the raiding done on the Scottish–English border by the border reivers
tent is a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A greedy raider is caught with red wine amid the loot.
explanation.walkthrough: Reive is a Scots word meaning to raid or plunder, used of the border reivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Retentive describes holding on tightly, so it shares the sense of grasping as clutching firmly.

clue.text: Active soldier fell in the drink

indicators.note: falling in something puts you inside it

blocks.note: ale is a drink
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A lively soldier tumbled into the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is slang for the sea, but here it is the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile means nimble and quick-moving, a close synonym for active.

clue.text: Diamond tricks

definitions.note: the whole clue doubles as a sly hint at the game

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for the card suit diamonds
arts are wiles or tricks

explanation.surface: Card play involving the diamond suit.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the puzzle's unstated games, clued by wordplay alone. Diamond and tricks both suggest bridge, but they build the pub game.
explanation.definitionFit: No words define it: throwing small missiles at a board is one of the puzzle's hidden set of pub sports and pastimes.

clue.text: Perjury?

blocks.note: surface reading: lying under oath
setter's reading: the offence the novelist Jeffrey Archer was jailed for in 2001, so the sort of thing Archer did

explanation.walkthrough: The British novelist and peer Jeffrey Archer was convicted of perjury in 2001; the sport's name reads as Archer-y, Archer's kind of behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: The sport of shooting with bow and arrow takes its name from an archer, which here suggests the topical politician and his crime.

clue.text: Defective crockery

definitions.note: the whole clue doubles as a joke on the game

blocks.note: defective means bad
Minton is a famous make of English china

explanation.surface: Chipped or faulty china.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the puzzle's unstated games, clued by wordplay alone. Minton is a Staffordshire pottery firm whose name is used for its china.
explanation.definitionFit: No words define it: the racket game played with a shuttlecock belongs to the puzzle's hidden set of sports and pastimes.

clue.text: Sense

blocks.note: surface reading: good judgment or sanity
setter's reading: the plural used in the idiom about losing one's wits, also the name of a children's game with glass balls

explanation.walkthrough: To lose your marbles is to go mad, so having them is having your wits; the word is also a children's game played with small glass balls.
explanation.definitionFit: In the informal idiom about losing your marbles, the word stands for sanity or common sense.

clue.text: A Minoan puzzled about all sorts of things

indicators.note: being puzzled about something means being muddled, so the letters are confused into a new order

blocks.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An ancient Cretan is baffled by a whole miscellany of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Omniana is a collection of miscellaneous notes or items, from Latin meaning things of every kind.

clue.text: Putting in crates

blocks.note: surface reading: packing goods into wooden containers
setter's reading: the same verb form names the sport of fighting with gloved fists

explanation.walkthrough: The verb for packing into cases is also the name of the fist-fighting sport, another game in the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: To box goods is to pack them into cases or crates, so the present participle means putting in crates.

clue.text: Wrong about cold fish eating a lizard

indicators.note: about means going around, so the first word surrounds the next
something eating another takes it inside itself

blocks.note: a sin is a wrong
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
the cod is a fish
a is read as one, the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Mistakenly the cold-blooded fish swallows a lizard.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves are containers: the cold letter sits inside the wrong, and the a sits inside the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Scincoid describes a skink or a skink-like reptile, so it names a kind of lizard.

clue.text: Having an argument

blocks.note: surface reading: quarrelling, said to rhyme with cow
setter's reading: the same spelling, said to rhyme with go, is the sport of propelling a boat with oars

explanation.walkthrough: The word for quarrelling rhymes with how; spelt identically and said like go, it is the water sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A row is a noisy quarrel, so being in the middle of one is quarrelling, which is having an argument.

clue.text: Silence

blocks.note: surface reading: quiet, or a call for it
setter's reading: an old word for hush, also the card game for four players in which silence was once expected

explanation.walkthrough: Whist is an archaic call meaning hush; the card game is thought to take its name from the quiet in which it was played.
explanation.definitionFit: As an old interjection or noun it means quiet or hush, exactly a command for silence.

clue.text: Clear one working during feast at midday

indicators.note: something during another event happens within it

blocks.note: a meal is a feast
to clear is to rid
Roman numeral one
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Clearing up after a lunchtime banquet while still at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Meridional relates to midday or noon, from the Latin for midday, and also to the south.

clue.text: One is a Moslem leader

blocks.note: one is read as I, and with is it gives I'm
a and an are both the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Somebody is a head of a Muslim congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as someone saying 'I'm an'.
explanation.definitionFit: Iman is a variant spelling of imam, the man who leads prayers in a mosque.

clue.text: Seychelles force doesn't start working together for gain

indicators.note: a word that does not start has lost its opening letter

blocks.note: SY is the international vehicle registration code for the Seychelles
energy is force or power

explanation.surface: An island nation's army stalls when trying to cooperate profitably.
explanation.definitionFit: Synergy is cooperation in which the combined effect exceeds the sum of separate efforts, so joint working brings a benefit.

clue.text: A wander round hospital waste holder

blocks.note: taken as written
to stray is to wander
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A stroll around the hospital grounds to find a rubbish bin.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashtray is a dish that receives cigarette ash, a kind of waste, so it holds waste.
